raw_response:
I've been working this land for forty years. My father worked it before me. I know what Quzhou soil wants, I know when the rains come and when they don't, and I know how much water the well can give me without running dry.

My 8.5 mu splits the way it always has — 5 mu rotates wheat and maize, 3.5 mu grows cotton. Cotton is hard work at my age, just me and my wife now, but it brings in cash and I know how to grow it. I won't change that.

For wheat, I plant in October after rotary tillage breaks up the maize stubble. I water three times: once before winter sets in to help the roots, once at jointing, once when the heads are filling. I put down about 14 jin of nitrogen per mu — that's what the fields have taken every year and the yields stay steady around 420 jin. No need to do more.

For maize, I go straight into the stubble after wheat harvest in June. No ploughing. I buy hybrid seed from the market in town, same brand as last year, it did well. Summer rains handle most of the water — I irrigate once if August gets dry. One spray for aphids, one for stem borer.

Cotton I plough deep in spring, plant in late April. Cotton needs the most from me — four waterings, five pesticide rounds for bollworm and spider mites. My hands know that work. Yield around 280 jin of seed cotton per mu is normal for me here.
